text:
Alex Kim: quick UX q — fallthrough / automatic fallback policy for rollouts. Thinking about how we surface degrade modes and triggers in the Console audit. Two options: show terse operator-friendly rows vs detailed event drilldowns.

Nora Patel: show raw error codes + counts (500/503/timeout) vs map to friendly reasons (backend-unavailable, rate-limited). Pros/cons? :thinking_face:

Chris Wang: I'd keep both: friendly label with a toggle to expand raw codes. Operators want quick context + ability to drill into raw events.

Maria Gomez: Also need to show sampling rate for telemetry + which requests were sampled. Otherwise audits look like magic. Maybe show "sampled 1.2%" and link to sample ids.

Alex Kim: rough compact row idea: [mode] [trigger summary] [last triggered at] [sample frac] [why summary]. Click expands to list of events (time, short path, error code). We should avoid showing full request bodies by default.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout r-20260323-14 triggered fallback -> mode: softfail, reason: 503 spike, sampled 12/1200 events, operator: Chris W :robot_face:

Nora Patel: retention + PII note — redact request payloads. Show a stable event hash + path + status. Provide "view raw" behind IAM if needed. Also show sampling policy used at time of trigger.

Chris Wang: API suggestion: return both computed_reason and raw_reasons array + sampling_meta. Example payload we can return from /audit/rollouts/:id/events?v=1:

```json
{"computed_reason":"503_spike","raw_reasons":[{"code":503,"count":98},{"code":"timeout","count":24}],"sampled":0.01,"sampled_ids":["evt_abc123","evt_def456"]}
```

Maria Gomez: UX copy idea: "Automatically fell back to lower-latency model due to high 503 rate — 1% of requests sampled." Short + human.

Alex Kim: ops/engineering practical Qs: 1) do we store full raw_reasons in audit index (cost), or compute on the fly from events? 2) sampling_metadata contract (seed, fraction, deterministic ids).

Chris Wang: prefer compute-on-write summary (counts) + keep sampled event list pointers for 30d. That keeps query fast and costs bounded. Will include sampling_seed in sampling_meta.

Nora Patel: UI affordance: small "why" pill that on hover shows breakdown + link to expand. Also a tiny icon explaining sampling and retention.

Alex Kim: privacy checklist: add redaction rules, retention (30d), IAM gating on raw view, and KMS log pointer if operator wants full decrypted payload.

Chris Wang: I'll prototype the endpoint + schema in a branch. Will add unit tests for redaction and sampling_meta.

Nora Patel: I'll mock a compact card + expanded drawer. Putting a quick Figma link in the doc later (internal).

Alex Kim: Awesome. Next steps: @Chris open a draft PR for schema, @Nora add mock screenshots to the RFC. I'll file the tiny RFC and add to the design sprint board. Thanks all :party_parrot:
